title: Symmetry of the derived tensor product
statement:
For a commutative ring $\Lambda$ and $A,B\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$
there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
A\kunotimes{\Lambda}B\cong B\kunotimes{\Lambda}A
$$

in $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, natural in $A$ and $B$.

proof.text: Work on the small etale site of the scheme $T$, with the constant commutative ring sheaf $R=\Lambda_T$. Choose the universe of module sheaves larger than that of the small etale site, so the smallness hypothesis of the descent theorem holds. Write $Q$ for derived localization. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to representing complexes for $A$ and $B$ to obtain K-flat resolutions $P$ and $N$ whose terms are flat. Thus they belong to the full homotopy subcategory $\mathcal P_R$ in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. That node gives canonical model isomorphisms $i_{P,N}:Q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RN)\xrightarrow{\sim}A\kunotimes{\Lambda}B$ and $i_{N,P}:Q\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes_RP)\xrightarrow{\sim}B\kunotimes{\Lambda}A$, natural on the resolving subcategory and compatible with inversion of its quasi-isomorphisms. This is the construction of [def-kun-derived-tensor] with both representing complexes chosen K-flat; no identification of etale and pro-etale coefficient categories is used.

proof.text: For any two complexes $P,N$, construct $c_{P,N}:\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RN)\to\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes_RP)$ by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ on the $(p,q)$ summand. The ordinary swap is well defined because $R$ is commutative: the balanced relation $rx\otimes y=x\otimes ry$ maps to $y\otimes rx=ry\otimes x$; it respects restrictions and hence sheafifies by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Extend these maps by the direct-sum universal property of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Its differential gives $d c(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{pq}d_Ny\otimes x+(-1)^{pq+q}y\otimes d_Px$, whereas $c d(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{(p+1)q}y\otimes d_Px+(-1)^{p+p(q+1)}d_Ny\otimes x$; the coefficients agree. Applying the swap twice multiplies by $(-1)^{pq+qp}=1$. For degree-zero complex maps $a:P\to P'$ and $b:N\to N'$, both routes in the naturality square send $x\otimes y$ to $(-1)^{pq}b(y)\otimes a(x)$. Thus $c$ is a natural chain isomorphism with inverse $c_{N,P}$. Passing these equations through $Q$ gives the corresponding equations on homotopy-category maps.

proof.text: Let $U(A,B)=A\kunotimes{\Lambda}B$ and $V(A,B)=B\kunotimes{\Lambda}A$. On pairs of resolving objects define $s_{QP,QN}=i_{N,P}\circ Q(c_{P,N})\circ i_{P,N}^{-1}$. The naturality just calculated and the natural model comparisons in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] make this a natural transformation between the restrictions of $U$ and $V$ to $\mathcal P_R\times\mathcal P_R$. Apply the last clause of that node to extend it uniquely to $s:U\to V$ on $D(R)\times D(R)$. Apply the same clause to the swapped inverse maps to obtain $t:V\to U$. Since $c_{N,P}c_{P,N}=1$, the restrictions of $ts$ and $st$ are identities; uniqueness of extension makes $ts=1_U$ and $st=1_V$ everywhere. Therefore every $s_{A,B}$ is an isomorphism, natural in both derived variables. Uniqueness also shows that any choices of K-flat resolutions give this same transformation under the canonical model comparisons. This supplies the required canonical symmetry, including the unbounded case.
